faqs.question: What is the ideal weight for daily wear gold jewellery?
faqs.answer: For comfortable all-day wear, gold earrings should weigh 2 to 4 grams, chains 3 to 6 grams, pendants 1 to 3 grams, and bangles 4 to 6 grams each. These weights provide the look and feel of real gold without any discomfort during extended wear. At Auric Jewels, our daily wear collection is curated within these weight ranges.

faqs.question: Is 18K or 22K gold better for office wear?
faqs.answer: 18K gold is generally more practical for daily office wear because it is more durable and scratch-resistant than 22K gold. It is also the preferred choice for diamond-studded pieces. However, for plain gold bangles and traditional designs, 22K gold offers a richer colour and higher purity. Both options are available at Auric Jewels with BIS hallmarking.

faqs.question: Can I wear gold jewellery every day without damaging it?
faqs.answer: Yes, gold is highly durable and suitable for daily wear. However, you should remove gold jewellery before swimming (chlorine can damage alloy metals in 18K gold), applying chemicals, or engaging in heavy physical activity. Regular cleaning and annual professional maintenance will keep your daily wear pieces in excellent condition for decades.

faqs.question: What are the most popular lightweight gold designs for working women in 2026?

Minimalist designs with clean lines are favoured for professional settings, while diamond-accented pieces add a touch of luxury without being overstated.

faqs.question: How do I choose between gold studs and diamond studs for daily wear?
faqs.answer: Gold studs offer a warm, classic look that pairs beautifully with Indian wear and professional attire. lab-grown-vs-natural-diamonds-comparison.seoTitle: Lab-Grown vs Natural Diamonds India 2026 | Auric Jewels Gurgaon

faqs.question: Are lab-grown diamonds real diamonds?
faqs.answer: Yes. Lab-grown diamonds are chemically, physically, and optically identical to natural diamonds. They are made of pure crystallised carbon and have the same hardness, brilliance, and fire as natural diamonds. The only difference is their origin — laboratory versus Earth's mantle.

faqs.question: Can a jeweller tell the difference between lab-grown and natural diamonds?
faqs.answer: Not with standard gemological tools. Lab-grown and natural diamonds look identical under a jeweller's loupe and even under standard microscopy. Only specialised equipment (such as a DiamondView or spectroscopy device) can detect the subtle growth patterns that distinguish the two. This is why certification from IGI or GIA is essential — it clearly identifies the diamond's origin.

faqs.question: Do lab-grown diamonds hold their value in India?
faqs.answer: Currently, lab-grown diamonds have very limited resale value in India. As production technology improves and supply increases, prices have declined steadily. Most established jewellers do not offer buyback or exchange on lab-grown diamonds. If long-term value retention is important to you, natural certified diamonds remain the recommended choice.

faqs.question: Which certification should I look for when buying diamonds in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: Look for IGI (International Gemological Institute) or GIA (Gemological Institute of America) certification. Both are internationally recognised and follow rigorous grading standards. At Auric Jewels, every diamond comes with verifiable IGI or GIA certification, and we encourage buyers to check their certificate numbers independently.

faqs.question: Is a lab-grown diamond suitable for an engagement ring?
faqs.answer: A lab-grown diamond is a real diamond and makes a beautiful engagement ring. However, if resale value, generational heirloom potential, or exchange value are important to you and your family, a natural diamond is the more practical choice for an engagement ring. In India, most families continue to prefer natural diamonds for engagement purposes.

faqs.question: What is the price difference between lab-grown and natural diamonds in 2026?
faqs.answer: Lab-grown diamonds are approximately 70 to 85 per cent less expensive than equivalent natural diamonds in India as of 2026. For example, a 1-carat G-colour VS1-clarity natural diamond priced at ₹3,00,000 to ₹4,50,000 would have a lab-grown equivalent at ₹45,000 to ₹90,000. This gap has widened in recent years and is expected to continue.

faqs.question: Is gold jewellery a good investment in 2026?
faqs.answer: Yes. Gold has delivered consistent long-term appreciation in India, averaging 10 to 12 per cent annually over the past decade. BIS hallmarked gold jewellery from a trusted jeweller like Auric Jewels combines investment value with wearability, cultural significance, and lifetime exchange potential — making it one of the most practical investment avenues for Indian families.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 22K and 24K gold for investment?
faqs.answer: 24K gold is 99.9 per cent pure and is used in coins and bars. It is too soft for jewellery. 22K gold is 91.6 per cent pure, with the remaining 8.4 per cent consisting of alloy metals that provide the strength needed for wearable jewellery. For investment in jewellery form, 22K gold offers the best combination of purity and durability.

faqs.question: Do making charges reduce the investment value of gold jewellery?
faqs.answer: Making charges are not recoverable at resale — you receive the prevailing gold value for the gold content. However, gold jewellery serves a dual purpose (adornment and investment) that coins and ETFs cannot match. For pure investment, gold coins have lower making charges. For jewellery that you will wear, gift, and pass down, the making charges are the cost of craftsmanship and design.

faqs.question: How can I verify that my gold jewellery is BIS hallmarked?
faqs.answer: Every BIS hallmarked piece carries a HUID (Hallmark Unique Identification) number that can be verified on the official BIS website (bis.gov.in) or through the BIS Care mobile app. Simply enter the HUID to confirm the purity, weight, and hallmarking centre details. At Auric Jewels, we provide the HUID documentation with every purchase.

faqs.question: Is Dhanteras or Akshaya Tritiya the best time to buy gold?
faqs.answer: Both days are considered highly auspicious for gold purchases in Hindu tradition. However, gold prices are market-driven and do not offer discounts on specific days. The best investment strategy is to buy gold when prices dip and spread purchases across the year. Auspicious days add cultural and spiritual value to your purchase, while strategic timing adds financial value.

faqs.question: Is platinum jewellery suitable for daily wear by men?
faqs.answer: Yes. Platinum is one of the most durable precious metals and is ideal for daily wear. Unlike gold, platinum does not lose metal when scratched — it displaces, meaning the metal moves rather than wears away. A platinum chain, bracelet, or ring can be worn every day for decades and still retain virtually all of its original weight and integrity.

faqs.question: How does platinum compare to silver in men's jewellery?
faqs.answer: Platinum and silver look similar in colour but differ dramatically in quality. Silver tarnishes, scratches easily, and is not suitable for long-term daily wear. Platinum is 30 times rarer than gold, does not tarnish, and is significantly more durable. For fine jewellery that will be worn regularly, platinum is in an entirely different category from silver.

faqs.question: What weight of platinum chain is recommended for men?
faqs.answer: For daily wear, a platinum chain weighing 15 to 25 grams offers a comfortable balance of substance and wearability. For a more prominent look, chains of 25 to 40 grams provide a bolder presence. The ideal weight depends on your build, personal style, and whether the chain will be worn under or over clothing.

faqs.question: Is platinum hypoallergenic?
faqs.answer: Yes. Platinum jewellery is typically 95 per cent pure, with only 5 per cent alloy metals (usually iridium or ruthenium, which are also hypoallergenic). This makes platinum the safest precious metal for men with sensitive skin or nickel allergies — a common concern with white gold, which often contains nickel in its alloy.

faqs.question: Does platinum jewellery require special maintenance?
faqs.answer: Platinum is remarkably low-maintenance. It does not tarnish, fade, or require re-plating like white gold. Over time, it develops a subtle matte patina that many wearers appreciate. To restore the original high shine, a simple professional polish at Auric Jewels — offered complimentary — brings the piece back to its original brilliance.

layered-necklace-styling-guide-indian-wo.seoTitle: Layered Necklace Styling Guide India | Auric Jewels Gurgaon

faqs.question: How many necklaces should I layer together?
faqs.answer: Two to three layers work best for everyday and professional settings. For evening wear, festivals, and weddings, three to four layers create a more dramatic effect. Avoid layering more than four necklaces — beyond that point, the look becomes cluttered rather than curated. The goal is intentional styling, not maximum quantity.

faqs.question: Can I layer necklaces of different gold purities (18K and 22K)?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can mix 18K and 22K gold in a layered arrangement. The slight colour difference (18K is lighter, 22K is warmer) adds subtle visual variety. Many women combine a 22K gold chain with an 18K diamond-accented pendant necklace for a beautiful contrast. At Auric Jewels, our collection includes pieces in both purities designed for complementary layering.

faqs.question: Do layered necklaces work with high necklines?
faqs.answer: High necklines limit the canvas for layering. With a turtleneck or high-neck blouse, wear a single long chain (22 inches or longer) over the fabric for a clean, modern look. Save multi-layer styling for lower necklines — V-necks, scoop necks, and open collars — where each layer is fully visible.

faqs.question: How do I prevent layered necklaces from tangling?
faqs.answer: Tangling is the most common challenge with layered necklaces. To minimise tangling: use necklaces of distinctly different lengths (at least 2 inches apart), choose chains of different thicknesses (thicker chains tangle less), and use a layering clasp — a multi-strand clasp that keeps all your necklaces separated at the back of the neck. Store layered necklaces separately when not wearing them.

faqs.question: What earrings pair best with layered necklaces?
faqs.answer: When wearing layered necklaces, keep earrings simple to avoid visual competition. Gold or diamond studs are the safest choice. Small hoops also work well. Avoid large statement earrings or heavy jhumkas when layering necklaces — let the neck be the focal point. The exception is minimalist two-layer styling, where slightly more prominent earrings can balance the look.
